title: Retire orch-sequential, harden backend errors, remove flat collect deadline, unify kill path
goal: Fix stage timeouts silently not applying by retiring the fallback orchestrator, making backend errors fatal, removing the 300 s flat collect deadline, bounding always_run stages by timeout_s:, and routing all process kills through the shared kill helper.

steps.description: Run grep -rl for orch-sequential, ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT, ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT, router.timeout_s, and _orch_local_kill_slot in tests/ to enumerate every test that pins these identifiers; all matches enter the scope of the steps that change them, as required by CLAUDE.md test scope discovery.

Write failing tests: a guard that fails when the orch-sequential plugin directory exists or any file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential, and a test that fails when a config naming sequential does not produce a misconfigured result; both must redden against the current tree before any implementation.

Delete the orch-sequential plugin directory and its capabilities golden file; remove its built-in lookup entry from the orchestrator backend loader so sequential and orch-sequential are treated as unknown names like any other; delete tests that tested the orch-sequential plugin itself (tests/unit/orch-sequential-test.sh); migrate each other test file that used orch-sequential as a behavioral fixture — including tests/integration/stage-time-limit-test.sh and tests/unit/map-strategy-test.sh — to run on orch-mock or bash-parallel so those tests still pass on the new backend (not merely have their orch-sequential references stripped); remove or replace all remaining orch-sequential references in wiki pages and plugin files (orch-mock, orch-ruflo-hive, plugin-artifact-goldens-test.sh G5 block) so the guard test stays green.

Write failing tests, exercised against the installed tree (install.sh layout), that confirm a missing backend and an unreadable backend config each produce a misconfigured run result naming the backend, with no silent fallback and no discarded warning; must fail at the merge-base.

Remove both fallback paths in the orchestrator backend loader — the not-found fallback that silently selected orch-sequential, and the config-unreadable path that discarded its warning — and replace both with a hard misconfigured failure that names the backend.

Write failing tests that plant a hang in a run hook dispatched through the orchestrator route (bash-parallel and mock backends, across map, fanout, and sequential-strategy configurations) and confirm the stage ends timed_out at its timeout_s:; also confirm that a stage whose timeout_s: exceeds 300 s completes without early termination; these must redden on main where ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT is still passed.

Remove the ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT argument from the collect calls in the map, fanout, and sequential-strategy files so the stage-level timeout_s: (already enforced by the lifecycle watchdog) is the only time bound on the orchestrator route.

Write failing tests confirming that the release and persist always_run stages are bounded by their timeout_s: values (30 s and 120 s) and that the model-call timeout field in the stage config is no longer consulted as a whole-stage deadline; must fail on main where router.timeout_s is still read for this purpose.

Remove the model-call timeout field read from the always_run dispatch path in the pipeline runner and replace the hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence there with a call to the shared process-group kill helper; move timeout_s: for release (30 s) and persist (120 s) from under the router: block to the top-level stage block in both shipped templates so template_stage_time_limit finds them.

Write a failing test confirming that when a hook spawns a child process that ignores SIGTERM, the kill path in the local engine slot terminates the child and leaves no orphan; must fail at the merge-base where the hand-rolled sequence is used.
Replace the hand-rolled TERM/0.5 s-wait/KILL sequence in the local engine slot killer with a call to the shared process-group kill helper, eliminating the second hand-rolled kill path.

Amend ADR-011 to record the orch-sequential retirement, the new default backend, and the hard-error rule for missing or unreadable backends; amend ADR-017 to record that router.timeout_s bounds only one model call; add an ## Enforced by entry to each amended statement naming the test from steps 2–11 that enforces it; remove ADR-011 and ADR-017 from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt so npm run lint accepts them without the baseline exemption.

Run npm test and npm run lint to confirm the full test suite and shellcheck pass, including all new guard tests, regression tests, and the migrated fixture tests, with no remaining references to retired identifiers outside permitted files.
